title: Catholic maritime ministry plans expanded port visit for seafarers and fishers support
summary: A ministry that caters to the concerns of seafarers, fishers, and their families has announced plans to expand its pastoral visits to more local and international ports, CBCP News reported.

blocks.text: A ministry that caters to the concerns of seafarers, fishers, and their families has announced plans to expand its pastoral visits to more local and international ports, CBCP News reported.

Fr. Jose Conrado Estafia, national director of Stella Maris Philippines, said maritime ministry of the Catholic Church aims to reach at least 38 ports and that this would be part of an agreement with the Bureau of Customs.
In an interview over Radyo Veritas, Estafia said most of the targeted ports are international to allow the Church to reach more Filipino maritime workers.
He also said there are plans to "strengthen support for migrant and local fishers, as well as families facing challenges linked to overseas employment."
“We will be with them, walk with them, and journey with them,” he said.
The report also said that the national Stella Maris also aim to bring seafarers’ concerns to the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) and the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW).
"The organization plans to expand mental health programs by working with psychologists and other specialists, drawing on research into seafarers’ psychological challenges and coping strategies."
The organization launched its website, stellamaris.ph, at a conference held in Dauis, Bohol that is aimed at expanding its evangelization and outreach through digital platforms. — BAP, GMA News
